rows.note: Use this as the everyday spoken noun for one computer-mouse click or button press; it is the all-purpose choice for the computing sense.

example.jyutping: gam6 jat1 haa5 zau6 hoi1 dou2 go3 mong5 jip6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for pressing a button or clicking a computer item, link, or website.

example.english: You can click this button to open the website.
example.traditional: 撳呢個掣就可以入到個網站。
example.jyutping: gam6 ni1 go3 zai3 zau6 ho2 ji5 jap6 dou2 go3 mong5 zaam6

rows.note: Use this for the brief sharp mechanical sound made by a lock, latch, switch, or similar object.

example.english: The lock turned with a click and opened.
example.traditional: 門鎖轉咗，咔一聲就開喇。
example.jyutping: mun4 so2 zyun2 zo2 kaa1 jat1 sing1 zau6 hoi1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for the social sense when two people get along well rather than for computer clicking.

example.english: I click well with my new colleagues, so working together is much easier.
example.traditional: 我同新同事相處得好，合作順利好多。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 san1 tung4 si6 soeng1 cyu5 dak1 hou2 hap6 zok3 seon6 lei6 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this when something suddenly makes sense or you suddenly realize the answer.

example.english: After you explained it, it did click for me all of a sudden.
example.traditional: 聽完你解釋，我突然明白喇。
example.jyutping: teng1 jyun4 nei5 gaai2 sik1 ngo5 dat6 jin4 ming4 baak6 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a device or object emitting a short clicking sound, especially when describing the sound itself.

example.english: The lock made a click when it shut.
example.jyutping: go3 so2 saan1 maai4 daap1 jat1 sing1
